newsitem.title: USA: Wis. Senate committee passes amended stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Wis. Senate committee passes amended stadium bill.

text.p: A Wisconsin Senate committee on Wednesday approved a compromise bill limiting the powers of the board overseeing the financing and construction of a new ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers American League baseball team, a committee clerk said.

The bill imposes fewer restrictions on the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District than the original proposal, said Phil Calabrese, clerk for the Judiciary, Campaign Finance Reform and Consumer Affairs Committee.

As proposed by state Sen. Joe Wineke, D-Verona, the bill would have set a $160 million bond limit for the district and limited its ability to enter into certain types of contracts, financial mechanisms or financial instruments, Calabrese said.

The amended bill eliminates the district's ability to issue bonds backed by the moral obligation of the state, requires quarterly financial disclosures to the co-chairs of the Wisconsin legislature's joint finance committee and an annual estimate on when a five-county sales tax used to back revenue bonds for the ballpark can be eliminated, Calabrese said.
The compromise bill is scheduled to be considered by the full Senate on Tuesday, Calabrese said.

District officials had called the original proposal unconstitutional and said that it could kill the $250 million project if it became law. They could not be reached immediately to comment on the new bill on Wednesday.
The original passed the Senate economic development committee in March, but was moved to the judiciary committee after several legal questions were raised.
